sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Mealf Wiki Mealf is a self-hosted household meal planner with an installable browser app (PWA). One backend container serves the PWA at /app/, the administration console at /, the API and a durable background worker. SQLite and private configuration live in one persistent /data volume. Cloudflare Tunnel or another HTTPS reverse proxy provides the public entry point. This is a development preview. Review the implementation status and the notes for the image or source revision you deploy. A feature documented from source may not yet be included in a published image. Live AI/Bring! compatibility and physical iPhone behaviour have not been established by synthetic or Linux browser tests.

sections.heading: Set up a new installation
sections.text: Set up a new installation Follow Installation to choose a prebuilt image or build from source. Configure Cloudflare Tunnel or an HTTPS reverse proxy. Complete First-run setup with your private setup token. Install the PWA and create your first recipe and meal. Set up backups before relying on stored household data. You need Docker Engine with Compose v2, persistent local storage and a valid HTTPS hostname. No Mac, App Store account or mandatory AI subscription is required.

sections.heading: Configure optional features
sections.text: Configure optional features Configuration: origins, time zones, proxy trust and server settings. AI recipe import: cloud OCR/extraction, configurable providers and review. Bring! integration: optional shopping-list synchronisation. Meal reminders: optional notifications on each browser device.

sections.heading: Operate the installation
sections.text: Operate the installation Backup and recovery: exports, sensitive backups and restoration. Upgrades and maintenance: updates, retention and rollback. Troubleshooting: common problems and safe diagnostic information. The household uses a shared account with independent device sessions. There are no default credentials or separate administrator roles. Keep the data volume, container logs, tunnel credentials and exports private. Never run two backend instances against the same SQLite volume. The product was previously called aircooker. Existing package, Compose, API and storage names retain that identifier for compatibility; do not rename volumes during an upgrade. See the branding and compatibility notes.

title: Installation
description: Save the complete configuration below as compose.yml in a folder on your Docker server. Replace https://mealf.example.com in BASEURL with your public HTTPS address.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: Installation Save the complete configuration below as compose.yml in a folder on your Docker server. Replace https://mealf.example.com in BASE_URL with your public HTTPS address. The :preview image tag tracks the latest published development preview. pull_policy: always checks for the newest image whenever you run docker compose up -d. Get the latest image and tags or read the latest release notes.

sections.heading: Full compose.yml
sections.text: Full compose.yml name: mealf-preview services: mealf: image: ghcr.io/cloudcookch/mealf-server:preview pull_policy: always restart: unless-stopped ports: - "5152:5152" environment: DATA_DIR: /data BASE_URL: https://mealf.example.com TZ: Europe/Zurich TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS: "" command: - /bin/sh - -c - | umask 077 exec python -m uvicorn aircooker.app:create_app \ --factory --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5152 \ --workers 1 --no-access-log \ --forwarded-allow-ips "$${TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS}" \ --timeout-graceful-shutdown 30 --limit-concurrency 64 healthcheck: test: - CMD - python - -c - "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:5152/api/v1/system/health', timeout=3)" interval: 30s timeout: 5s start_period: 15s retries: 3 volumes: - mealf-data:/data read_only: true tmpfs: - /tmp:size=64m,mode=1777 cap_drop: - ALL security_opt: - no-new-privileges:true pids_limit: 100 mem_limit: 512m stop_grace_period: 40s volumes: mealf-data:  Download compose.yml

sections.heading: Start Mealf
sections.text: Start Mealf Run these commands in the folder containing compose.yml: docker compose up -d docker compose logs --tail=100 mealf  This configuration runs Mealf on port 5152 and stores your data in the mealf-data volume. Keep that volume when updating. Point your Cloudflare Tunnel at http://127.0.0.1:5152 if its connector runs on the Docker host. If the connector runs elsewhere, use http://YOUR_SERVER_LAN_IP:5152 with your Docker server’s reachable LAN address. Publish mealf.example.com (or your own hostname) without a path, matching BASE_URL. Open https://mealf.example.com, enter the one-time setup_token from the private logs, and complete First-run setup. The app is at /app/.

sections.heading: Update to the latest preview
sections.text: Update to the latest preview Back up your data, then run docker compose up -d again in the same folder. Compose pulls the latest preview and recreates the container when its image changes. Keep your existing project name, volume, port, command and healthcheck settings.

title: First-run setup
description: Before creating an account, start the backend, configure HTTPS and set BASEURL to the exact public origin, such as https://mealf.example.com. The console at / and the PWA at /app/

sections.heading: First-run setup
sections.text: First-run setup Before creating an account, start the backend, configure HTTPS and set BASE_URL to the exact public origin, such as https://mealf.example.com. The console at / and the PWA at /app/ share that origin. See Installation.

sections.heading: Find the one-time setup token
sections.text: Find the one-time setup token While no household exists, each backend startup writes a setup_required log entry with setup_token. Read it in your container manager's private Logs view, or use: docker compose -f compose.yml logs --tail=100 mealf  Alternatively, read the restricted file from the running container: docker compose -f compose.yml exec mealf cat /data/config/setup-token  For a source build, use docker compose logs aircooker and docker compose exec aircooker cat /data/config/setup-token. Do not paste the token or unredacted startup logs into support issues. Set LOG_SETUP_TOKEN=false in the backend's Compose environment if you prefer file-only retrieval, then recreate the container. The token remains available in the file until successful setup.

sections.heading: Create the household
sections.text: Create the household Open the public HTTPS origin in your browser. You can also choose Open your kitchen from the PWA onboarding screen. Enter the setup token. Choose your own username and password. The password must contain at least 12 characters. There is no default account. Enter a household name and an IANA time zone, for example Europe/Zurich or Europe/Berlin. Choose the household language where offered. Complete setup, sign in and open /app/. Setup creates one household transactionally and then locks. The setup-token file is removed and the token cannot be reused. Configured starts stop logging it, although historical log records remain. Public registration is not available after setup.

sections.heading: Review the initial settings
sections.text: Review the initial settings At /, open Household to verify the name, time zone and default language. The household time zone controls meal dates, shopping-week boundaries and reminder times. The container's TZ variable does not replace it. Changing the displayed English/German UI language is separate from saving the household default. Open Account to review device sessions. The shared account has household-wide access; there are no separate administrator roles. Each device/browser has its own revocable session. Changing the password revokes all sessions, including your own. AI, Bring! and notifications are optional; configure them only when needed.

sections.heading: Recover a forgotten password
sections.text: Recover a forgotten password A local Docker administrator can run the interactive recovery command: docker compose -f compose.yml exec -it mealf python -m aircooker.cli recover  For a source build: docker compose exec -it aircooker python -m aircooker.cli recover  Enter the new password twice when prompted. Recovery changes the password and revokes all device/browser sessions. Sign in again afterward. There is no public email-reset endpoint. Do not delete the database, token file or volume to recover an existing account. If setup reports that the household already exists, sign in with that account or use local recovery. If a restart unexpectedly offers setup again, stop and verify that the original /data volume is mounted before creating another household. Source: administration and deployment.

title: Cloudflare Tunnel
description: Cloudflare Tunnel can expose Mealf over HTTPS without forwarding an inbound router port. The operator runs a cloudflared connector separately from the Mealf backend. Browser reques

sections.heading: Cloudflare Tunnel
sections.text: Cloudflare Tunnel Cloudflare Tunnel can expose Mealf over HTTPS without forwarding an inbound router port. The operator runs a cloudflared connector separately from the Mealf backend. Browser requests travel through Cloudflare and the connector to the backend's private HTTP listener. Keep Mealf's account authentication enabled. You need a Cloudflare account, a domain managed in that account, permission to create a tunnel/public hostname and a Docker host with outbound connectivity to Cloudflare. Follow Cloudflare's current connector installation instructions for supported platforms and tunnel firewall requirements. The connector's outbound tunnel connection is separate from the browser's HTTPS connection.

sections.heading: Choose where the connector runs
sections.text: Choose where the connector runs Connector location Public hostname's service URL Backend exposure On the Docker host http://127.0.0.1:5152 Published port 5152 on the Docker host In a separate container http://mealf:5152 for preview Compose Shared private Docker network; the published host port remains 127.0.0.1 inside a connector container refers to that connector, so it will not reach Mealf. For a source-build deployment the backend service name is aircooker, making the container target http://aircooker:8080.

sections.heading: Create the tunnel and hostname
sections.text: Create the tunnel and hostname In Cloudflare Zero Trust, open the Cloudflare Tunnels area under Networks/Connectors and create a Cloudflared tunnel, for example mealf. Choose the host or Docker connector option. Treat the supplied tunnel token as a credential. Follow the dashboard's platform installation instructions privately. Add a published application/public hostname such as mealf.example.com. Choose HTTP for the service and use the address from the table above. Leave the path empty so /, /app/ and /api/ all reach the same backend. Confirm the dashboard creates the hostname's DNS route. Resolve any existing conflicting DNS record instead of creating two competing routes. Set Mealf's BASE_URL to https://mealf.example.com and recreate its container. For this site’s compose.yml, edit BASE_URL under environment; for a source build, edit the environment in compose.yaml. See Configuration. The public connection uses HTTPS; HTTP is used only for the private connector-to-backend hop. Keep both on the same host/private Docker network for these examples. Do not disable TLS verification when configuring a different HTTPS origin service.

sections.heading: Option A: connector installed on the host
sections.text: Option A: connector installed on the host Keep the 5152:5152 port binding from the installation guide and configure the tunnel service as http://127.0.0.1:5152. Start the connector using the dashboard's instructions for your host OS, including its service/start-on-boot option. Tunnel credentials belong to that host service, not the Mealf image or application settings. Run this on the Docker host to check the private origin before testing the tunnel: curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:5152/api/v1/system/health  It should return {"status":"ok"}. Local HTTP health checks do not establish that browser login works; test the public HTTPS URL too. Forwarded-header trust must match the peer seen by the backend. Docker port forwarding can make a host connector appear as the bridge gateway rather than 127.0.0.1. Confirm that address from your network configuration before setting TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS. Leave trust empty until verified; never use or trust all networks. Without proxy trust, client-address rate limits may be shared across tunnel users. Option B provides an explicit connector address when you want a predictable Docker setup.

sections.heading: Option B: connector in Docker
sections.text: Option B: connector in Docker This example extends preview Compose without changing its existing volume or project name. For an existing installation, keep using the same installation directory and compose.yml. Stop any host connector for this tunnel before switching methods. For this optional two-file connector configuration, create a private .env file beside compose.yml for the connector image and token. Keep BASE_URL in compose.yml: CLOUDFLARED_IMAGE=cloudflare/cloudflared:REPLACE_WITH_REVIEWED_VERSION CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN=REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_TUNNEL_TOKEN  Replace both placeholders. Select a published cloudflared version supported by Cloudflare, or pin its immutable image digest. Obtain the token from the tunnel's connector setup screen, not from a general Cloudflare account API key. Restrict .env to the operator (chmod 600 .env) and exclude it from Git and support bundles. Docker administrators can inspect container environment values; treat them as trusted operators. Save the following as compose.tunnel.yaml next to compose.yml: services: mealf: environment: TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS: "172.30.85.2" networks: tunnel: ipv4_address: 172.30.85.3 cloudflared: image: ${CLOUDFLARED_IMAGE:?Set a reviewed cloudflared image} restart: unless-stopped command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run environment: TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN:?Set the tunnel token privately} networks: tunnel: ipv4_address: 172.30.85.2 read_only: true tmpfs: - /tmp:size=32m,mode=1777 cap_drop: [ALL] security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true] pids_limit: 100 mem_limit: 128m networks: tunnel: ipam: config: - subnet: 172.30.85.0/24  The subnet is an example. Check existing host, VPN and Docker networks first. If it overlaps, choose an unused private subnet and change the subnet, both service IPs and trusted proxy address together. Both addresses are fixed to avoid allocation collisions. Trust only the connector's IP. The network needs outbound access, so do not mark it internal: true without providing another outbound route. Set the public hostname's service URL to http://mealf:5152, then start both services: docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.tunnel.yaml up -d docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.tunnel.yaml ps docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.tunnel.yaml logs --tail=50 cloudflared  Keep both -f arguments for future operations on this installation. The published backend port remains available for local health checks; the connector does not need a published port. Do not launch the base Compose file as a second project against the same data volume. Source-build users can adapt the overlay's mealf service key and tunnel service URL to aircooker, retaining their original source Compose volume.

sections.heading: Cache, access and request settings
sections.text: Cache, access and request settings Add a Cloudflare cache rule that bypasses caching for the Mealf hostname. Do not apply a Cache Everything rule to authenticated API, console or media responses. The PWA maintains its own browser cache for public application files. Keep HTML/JavaScript rewriting, such as Rocket Loader, disabled for this hostname. Preserve the backend's content security policy and response headers. Preserve the hostname and normal forwarding headers. Do not rewrite requests onto another public origin or a path prefix. No WebSocket configuration is required. Interactive Cloudflare Access login or WAF challenges can interrupt API requests, installed-app use and native clients. Validate those flows before adding an extra access layer; Mealf does not implement Cloudflare service-token authentication. Cloudflare plan limits may reject uploads below Mealf's 280 MiB archive allowance. For large restores, use an HTTPS ingress that supports the required size, or a supported smaller transfer. Never expose an unauthenticated restore route.

sections.heading: Verify the installation
sections.text: Verify the installation Open https://mealf.example.com/api/v1/system/health, then / and /app/. Complete First-run setup, sign in, save a test recipe and reload. Confirm the tunnel remains connected after restarting the connector. An HTTP health response alone does not verify cookies, CSRF, uploads or PWA installation. A Cloudflare 502 usually means the connector cannot reach the configured private origin. Check the service name, network, port and backend health. A tunnel unavailable/1033 error points to connector availability or routing. A browser 403 after the page loads usually needs an exact BASE_URL, cookie/CSRF or edge-policy check. See Troubleshooting. This is a documented deployment pattern; no live Cloudflare account/tunnel was exercised while preparing these guides. Source: deployment and Cloudflare's remotely managed tunnel guide.

title: HTTPS & reverse proxy
description: Mealf needs a valid HTTPS origin for browser authentication and PWA installation. Set BASEURL to that exact origin, for example https://mealf.example.com, without /app/ or another

sections.heading: HTTPS & reverse proxy
sections.text: HTTPS and reverse proxy Mealf needs a valid HTTPS origin for browser authentication and PWA installation. Set BASE_URL to that exact origin, for example https://mealf.example.com, without /app/ or another path. A non-default HTTPS port, if used, is part of the origin. Serve the console, PWA and API on that same origin. Use Cloudflare Tunnel or your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The installation guide’s compose.yml publishes port 5152. Its host-installed proxy target is 127.0.0.1:5152. Source-build configurations may retain port 8080. Keep normal certificate verification enabled.

sections.heading: Host-installed Caddy example
sections.text: Host-installed Caddy example Point your hostname's DNS at the reverse proxy and arrange certificate issuance using your chosen Caddy deployment. Install a current supported Caddy version. The backend should be reachable from that host at 127.0.0.1:5152. mealf.example.com { @archive path /api/v1/admin/import/archive request_body @archive { max_size 280MiB } @jsonRestore path /api/v1/admin/import request_body @jsonRestore { max_size 8MiB } @uploads path /api/v1/media/ /api/v1/import-sources/ request_body @uploads { max_size 9MiB } @ordinary not path /api/v1/admin/import/archive /api/v1/admin/import /api/v1/media/ /api/v1/import-sources/ request_body @ordinary { max_size 1500000 } reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:5152 }  Replace the hostname, validate the Caddy configuration and reload using your host's service-management procedure. If the reverse proxy is another container, place both services on an appropriate private network and use mealf:5152 (preview) or aircooker:8080 (source build). Its own 127.0.0.1 will not reach the backend container. The import-source route is available only in images containing the AI media-import feature. Keeping its ingress allowance does not enable a missing backend feature.

sections.heading: Forwarded headers and proxy trust
sections.text: Forwarded headers and proxy trust Have the proxy preserve the public host and forward the original scheme and client IP. Set TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS to only the actual proxy peer address(es) or controlled proxy range seen by Uvicorn. An empty value is the default. Never use on public ingress. Host-to-container traffic can appear as a Docker bridge gateway; do not assume that a host-installed proxy appears as loopback inside the container. For a container proxy, a fixed address on a dedicated network provides a predictable peer. The Cloudflare Docker example shows this pattern. Do not trust an entire LAN or all private networks merely to make forwarding work. Recreate the backend after changing its environment.

sections.heading: Request limits
sections.text: Request limits Request Backend limit Proxy allowance in the example Ordinary JSON/API writes 1,500,000 bytes 1,500,000 bytes Recipe photos and AI source uploads 8 MiB source, with bounded request overhead 9 MiB Household JSON import 8 MiB 8 MiB Household ZIP import 280 MiB 280 MiB Keep limits specific to their routes. Increasing the proxy allowance does not raise the application's own limit. Add suitable read timeouts and ingress rate limits for your host; an AI call can take up to its configured timeout. There is no required WebSocket or streaming ingress. An external CDN may impose a lower upload ceiling.

sections.heading: Verify browser access
sections.text: Verify browser access Visit /api/v1/system/health on the public HTTPS hostname. Visit / and /app/ and sign in using that same hostname. Save a test recipe and check that it survives reload. If you will use them, test image upload and a private export/import in your environment. Session cookies are always Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict. Unsafe cookie requests also need the configured Origin and CSRF token. Do not strip cookies or Origin headers, split the API onto a second hostname, or disable these checks to fix login. See Troubleshooting for 401/403 and certificate errors. Source: deployment and security model.

title: Configuration
description: Mealf has two kinds of settings: container environment values controlled by the operator, and household/integration settings saved through the application. Changing the container t

sections.heading: Configuration
sections.text: Configuration Mealf has two kinds of settings: container environment values controlled by the operator, and household/integration settings saved through the application. Changing the container time zone or an environment default does not overwrite saved household settings.

sections.heading: Container settings
sections.text: Container settings Variable Default Configure it for DATA_DIR /data Persistent local state; keep the Docker volume mounted here BASE_URL https://localhost Exact public HTTPS origin, with no application path TZ Image setting Process time zone; household planning has its own saved IANA time zone TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS Empty Actual ingress proxy peers; never universal trust LOG_LEVEL info Server logging; avoid third-party debug logs that can disclose content LOG_SETUP_TOKEN true Whether an unconfigured startup prints its one-time token The installation guide’s compose.yml sets backend values directly under the service’s environment: section. Edit BASE_URL, TZ and any verified TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS there. An .env file is not required for this configuration. Its image uses the moving :preview tag with pull_policy: always; run docker compose up -d to fetch updates. The explicit command and healthcheck both use port 5152. For the source-build compose.yaml, edit the literal environment values in that file or use an explicit Compose override. After changes, use docker compose ... up -d with the same files/project to recreate the container. A plain restart does not load changed environment values. Preserve the volume and keep only one backend process.

sections.heading: Household and account
sections.text: Household and account At the administration console (/): Household saves the name, IANA time zone and default language. Account lists device sessions and lets you revoke sessions or change the password. AI saves optional provider profiles and the selected default model. Bring! connects credentials and selects an existing list. Data downloads portable exports and imports compatible JSON/ZIP files. The console is available in English and German. Its display-language selector is separate from the saved household language. The shared household account has access to these settings; there is no separate administrator-role system. In the PWA (/app/), Settings also contains AI configuration, device display choices, storage/sync recovery, household meal-suggestion preferences and per-device reminders. Save shared preferences while connected. Reminder drafts remain local until explicitly saved. See PWA and offline use and Meal reminders.

sections.heading: AI settings and precedence
sections.text: AI settings and precedence The application can save Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter and custom OpenAI-compatible profiles. Legacy text adapters for Anthropic, Ollama and OpenWebUI remain available. Model names are administrator-supplied; no model version is guessed. Capabilities must be enabled for the selected model. See AI recipe import. Saved encrypted settings override AI environment settings. A saved disabled state also overrides them. Changing AI_MODEL in Compose will therefore not replace a saved profile. Inspect the reported configuration origin and edit the application setting. Optional AI variable Default / meaning AI_PROVIDER Unset: disabled; supported provider identifier AI_BASE_URL Provider default; required for a custom compatible API AI_MODEL Required when AI is enabled; exact supported model ID AI_API_KEY_FILE Private regular key file readable by the backend; no group/world permissions or symlink AI_INPUT_FORMATS text; comma-separated supported capabilities, without spaces AI_TIMEOUT 30; valid range 1–120 seconds AI_MAX_CONTENT 50000; valid range 100–100000 UTF-8 bytes for text AI_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR 20; valid range 1–1000, shared by imports and probes AI_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT 0; set 1 only after verifying model/API JSON support AI_ALLOW_LOCAL_HTTP 0; explicit opt-in for a trusted self-hosted HTTP API For key-file deployments, mount the file read-only with restrictive permissions that permit UID 10001 to read it. Standard secret-file defaults may be too permissive for this check. Do not put keys in an endpoint URL or recipe, and do not disable public TLS verification. Application-managed keys are encrypted server-side and never returned to the browser.

sections.heading: Persistent state
sections.text: Persistent state Path under /data Purpose database/aircooker.sqlite3 and WAL/SHM Household records, sync history and durable jobs media/ Recipe photos jobs/ Protected temporary export/restore files backups/ Operator-created local snapshots config/setup-token One-time bootstrap token, removed after setup config/integrations.key Installation encryption key; required to decrypt saved integrations config/ai-provider.enc Saved encrypted AI settings and profiles config/bring.enc Encrypted Bring! connection settings config/webpush-vapid.enc Encrypted installation Web Push private key Some files exist only after their feature is configured. Raw AI import sources are private server state, separate from recipe photos, with bounded retention. Back up the whole volume for disaster recovery; a household export intentionally excludes credentials. Never delete encryption keys as a configuration-reset technique. Source: deployment, administration and AI configuration implementation.

title: PWA & offline use
description: Mealf's primary client is the installable browser app at your public HTTPS origin's /app/ path. The administration console remains at /. Use the same origin for the client and API;

sections.heading: PWA & offline use
sections.text: PWA and offline use Mealf's primary client is the installable browser app at your public HTTPS origin's /app/ path. The administration console remains at /. Use the same origin for the client and API; see Installation and HTTPS and reverse proxy.

sections.heading: Install on a device
sections.text: Install on a device Open https://mealf.example.com/app/ and sign in with the household account. On iPhone/iPad, use Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen, then open the new icon. On a supported desktop/Android browser, use its Install app option. Open the app online once and let it synchronise. View photos you will need offline. In Settings, request persistent browser storage where supported. Browsers can refuse the request or later evict data, so keep exports and synchronise regularly. A QR code can contain the public HTTPS app URL for easy opening. It must not contain passwords, setup tokens or session secrets. The optional demo has a separate local database and does not create or populate a real household.

sections.heading: Use recipes and the calendar
sections.text: Use recipes and the calendar Create or edit recipes in Recipes. Ingredients support explicit amounts, fractions and ranges; leave unknown quantities blank rather than inventing measurements. Recipe details can scale ingredient quantities to the chosen servings. Review every import before saving; see AI recipe import for media and provider requirements. Calendar supports Day, 3 days and Week views. Move meals by their grip or use the meal menu's move form. Multi-day views scroll horizontally. Week options copy plans or apply saved templates; copying does not duplicate already cooked leftovers. Record leftover portions and schedule them without overbooking the available amount. Pantry staples marked available are excluded from Bring! requirements. Include in shopping this week overrides this for the household's current Monday–Sunday week. Meal suggestions use the cached recipe library, ratings, history, variety and leftovers without AI. Shared suggestion preferences apply after an online save. Proposed plans remain previews until you explicitly approve them.

sections.heading: What works offline
sections.text: What works offline Recipes, meals, pantry, leftovers, templates, editor drafts, import requests, selected photos and outgoing changes are held in the browser's IndexedDB. Local edits survive reload and wait for foreground synchronisation. An unseen server photo may be unavailable offline. AI extraction, website fetching, initial sign-in, integration changes and new notification connections need the backend/network. The service worker caches only public build files. It does not cache authenticated API responses or private media; private records/photos use the app's separate local database. Offline storage is private content on the device, not an encrypted native Keychain.

sections.heading: Synchronisation and conflicts
sections.text: Synchronisation and conflicts Sync runs while the app is open, when reconnecting/returning to the foreground and periodically while visible. It does not depend on iPhone Background Sync. Once a change reaches the backend, durable import/Bring! jobs continue even if the browser closes. Watch the status bar for pending, offline or rejected work. Server commit order determines accepted updates, rather than device clocks. A permanent failure for one photo/recipe can block that item while other changes continue. Review the rejection in Settings; recover the affected recipe as a new copy or retain the server version where offered. Do not clear browser storage to resolve a blocked queue. After a server database restore, the app can detect changed history and stop old queued changes. Recover server history explicitly archives local records and queued work before adopting an anchored server snapshot. Recipe copies can be restored from these archives; reconstruction of other archived record types remains manual.

sections.heading: Preserve work before recovery or an update
sections.text: Preserve work before recovery or an update Use Export unsynchronised work in Settings before changing devices, clearing site data or attempting recovery. This browser recovery JSON includes local records, queued edits, drafts, archives and available photos, but no session or integration keys. Store it privately. It supports inspection/manual recovery; it is not the server household archive and is not automatically reimported. A server backup cannot contain edits that have never left an offline device. For a PWA update, finish active edits, accept the update prompt and close/reopen the installed app as needed. Do not uninstall or clear storage with pending work. An OS icon may stay cached longer than the page. Signing out revokes the session and hides retained work; it does not erase or encrypt browser storage. Remote revocation cannot remove data from a disconnected device.

sections.heading: Platform limits
sections.text: Platform limits Optional meal reminders require permission, connectivity and supported browser services. The PWA does not provide offline local alarms, native Share extensions, WidgetKit widgets, native biometric locking or passkeys. Physical iPhone/Safari behaviour and live push delivery remain unverified by the Linux/Chromium tests. Source: PWA guide, mobile calendar and planning preferences.

title: AI recipe import
description: For a new server, complete Installation and First-run setup first. See Configuration for container settings and Troubleshooting for deployment/login problems.

sections.heading: AI recipe import
sections.text: AI Recipe Import For a new server, complete Installation and First-run setup first. See Configuration for container settings and Troubleshooting for deployment/login problems. Mealf imports recipes from photographs, screenshots, PDFs, public recipe pages, supplied text, and supported cooking videos. Cloud vision performs OCR and recipe understanding; no OCR daemon, separate worker service, GPU, or additional Docker container is needed. Every import is a draft. Review the title, servings, ingredients, quantities, units, preparation/cooking/total times, and ordered instructions before saving. Missing facts remain unknown, and extraction issues appear in the editor. AI output is not a food safety, allergen, nutrition, or dietary certification.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: Architecture flowchart LR PWA[PWA: source and explicit consent] --> Upload[Authenticated private upload] PWA --> Queue[SQLite durable import queue] Upload --> Queue Queue --> Metadata[Website Schema.org Recipe JSON-LD] Metadata -->|Complete recipe| Draft[Editable preview] Metadata -->|Missing or unstructured, with consent| AI[Common AI provider interface] Queue -->|Image, PDF, supported video| AI AI --> Validate[Bounded provider-neutral schema validation] Validate --> Draft Draft -->|User edits and confirms| Sync[Existing transactional recipe and sync APIs]  The FastAPI modular monolith remains a single process with one SQLite writer. The existing durable queue performs extraction independently of an open browser. Requests retain replay fingerprints, cancellation/confirmation guards, and restore-aware sync checkpoints. The PWA can queue a source offline in IndexedDB; after reconnection it uploads the source before submitting the import. Closing the browser after submission does not cancel the job. For websites, complete Schema.org Recipe JSON-LD takes precedence even when AI is enabled for that import. No provider request or AI quota is consumed in that case. If metadata is missing/incomplete, AI is used only when enabled and explicitly consented to. A failed or private source is not silently replaced with fabricated content or fetched through an authenticated scraping service. The uploaded Mealf schema bundle is preserved under contracts/recipe-import/ as reference schemas and examples. recipe_extraction.py implements its schemaVersion: "1.0.0" extraction envelope with additional resource bounds and range validation. Unknown values are null, not guessed defaults; original ingredient and quantity text remain available. All provider adapters return ExtractionResult, independently of their native wire format. The backend validates the result even when a provider offers structured output. The existing canonical recipe/sync shape is extended additively: times, language, yield_info, category, cuisine, tags, ingredient annotations, instruction_details, and schema_version. Existing ingredient UUIDs and recipe mutation/ownership rules remain server/client responsibilities, never model output. The full extraction stays with the import draft; provider/model audit records are separate from recipe content. Incomplete extractions open an editor with blank missing fields. They cannot be confirmed until the required recipe facts are entered. Existing non-AI website imports retain their explicit serving-default review warning for compatibility.

sections.heading: Configure a provider
sections.text: Configure a provider Sign in to the PWA, open Settings → AI recipe import, and enable extraction. The administration console at / also provides the configuration under Optional AI extraction. Mealf currently uses its existing shared household account for administration; it does not introduce a new role or a public registration mechanism. Select a provider. Google Gemini is the initial provider option. AI stays disabled until configured; there is no bundled credential or hardcoded model version. Enter the API base URL, exact model identifier from that provider, and API key. Enable only input formats supported by that particular model and account. Text is always enabled. A provider's capabilities do not imply every model supports every format. Set the hourly request limit and timeout. Enable structured JSON output only if the selected model/API supports it. Choose Save as default. This selects the default provider/model for new imports. Provider profiles, including model, capabilities and credential, are retained independently. Switch back to a saved provider to reuse its profile. A blank key retains the saved key only for the same provider and endpoint. Changing the endpoint clears the old key unless you supply another; Remove this provider’s saved key explicitly clears it. Disabling AI retains profiles while stopping extraction. Stored keys are never displayed or returned. The console's Test saved AI configuration action sends a small synthetic text recipe. It consumes quota and may incur charges. A successful text probe does not verify vision, PDFs, video, or every model capability. The import preview is the relevant functional check for a particular source format.

sections.heading: Can I use my ChatGPT or Gemini subscription?
sections.text: Can I use my ChatGPT or Gemini subscription? Mealf's implemented cloud adapters authenticate with API keys. Signing into the ChatGPT or Gemini consumer app does not configure an API key or enable Mealf extraction. OpenAI: API billing is separate from ChatGPT subscriptions. OpenAI also supports subscription allowance sharing in eligible participating apps through Sign in with ChatGPT; the optional personal ChatGPT text-import connection implements that separate flow with a desktop helper and session-owned authorization. Do not use browser cookies, consumer account passwords or tokens copied from another tool as an API credential. Gemini: create a Gemini API project/key in Google AI Studio. Its free tier supports certain models within account/model quotas; paid usage uses the project's separate Cloud Billing configuration. A consumer subscription is not itself the API credential. Any subscription credit benefit depends on Google's current eligibility and supported services. For a first test, create a free-tier Gemini API key if available for your account/region, select an available model with the required input formats, enter the key in Mealf settings, save, and run the saved-configuration test in the console. Then import one non-sensitive sample recipe and review it before Save. Local English/German photo OCR remains available without a cloud account. Never paste the key into support chats or issues. Checked 2026-10-22 against the providers' official documentation: OpenAI API billing, ChatGPT in participating apps, Gemini API billing and free tier, and Gemini API keys.

sections.heading: Google Gemini
sections.text: Google Gemini Setting Value Provider gemini API base URL https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta Model Exact current model ID from Google AI Studio; enter it in settings Available adapter formats Text, image, PDF, video upload, public YouTube URL Create a Google AI Studio project and generate an API key at Google AI Studio. Review the project's billing, quota, region and data-use terms. Restrict the key to the required API where supported, then enter it in Mealf settings. Do not paste keys into recipe text or browser source code. The adapter uses generateContent with native inline media, a separate system instruction, JSON output, and optional responseJsonSchema. A model must support the formats you enable. For video, Mealf requests only the first ten minutes, sampled at one frame per second. This is a bounded import, not a full-length transcription service.

sections.heading: OpenAI
sections.text: OpenAI Setting Value Provider openai API base URL https://api.openai.com/v1 Model Configurable model ID with the required vision/document capabilities Available adapter formats Text, image, PDF on models supporting native file input Create a project key in the OpenAI API platform. Configure project permissions and billing limits, then enter the key in Mealf. A ChatGPT subscription is not an API credential or API billing plan. The adapter uses Chat Completions: images are image_url data URLs; PDFs are native file content parts. Enable PDF only when the selected model and endpoint document that contract. The adapter bounds completion tokens and validates JSON locally. Native video parts and YouTube URLs are not sent to this adapter; use supported images or supply a transcript.

sections.heading: OpenRouter
sections.text: OpenRouter Setting Value Provider openrouter API base URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 Model Exact model slug, including its organization prefix Available adapter formats Text, image, PDF when supported by the selected route Create a key at OpenRouter API keys. Fund/configure the account and key spending limits. Review the selected upstream provider's privacy and format support as well as OpenRouter's. Enter the key and model slug in Mealf settings. The adapter uses OpenAI-compatible content parts. PDF support depends on the route's native file handling; Mealf does not silently enable paid parsing plugins or switch upstream models to overcome incompatibility. Configure a compatible route or provide images/text.

sections.heading: Custom OpenAI-compatible APIs
sections.text: Custom OpenAI-compatible APIs Select openai-compatible, enter the complete API base URL (usually ending in /v1), and obtain a credential from that service's administrator. Mealf appends /chat/completions. Supply the exact served model identifier; newer model names require no application update. Use HTTPS with a certificate trusted by the container. The existing Allow HTTP for a trusted self-hosted endpoint option is an explicit administrator opt-in for an internal service; it is not a certificate-verification bypass. Configure private DNS/routing and an appropriate trust chain in the deployment. Do not send a cloud key to an unrelated custom endpoint. Legacy Anthropic/Ollama/OpenWebUI text configurations remain supported; this feature does not enable native media for those legacy adapters.

sections.heading: Docker and environment configuration
sections.text: Docker and environment configuration The existing Dockerfile builds the PWA and packages the Python modules and SQL migration. Rebuild and restart the existing service, preserving the /data volume: docker compose up --build -d  The existing Photo or screenshot camera/chooser remains a local English/German OCR path and sends only recognized text when optional AI is selected. The attachment field under Link or text is the separate path that sends a file to the configured AI model, after explicit consent and capability checks. Both paths require review before saving. No additional dependency or service is required. Migration 011_recipe_import.sql creates the private upload and AI-attempt tables and adds extraction data to import drafts. Released migrations are unchanged. Standard household JSON/ZIP exports contain reviewed recipes and their new metadata; they exclude provider credentials and transient source uploads. Saved application settings take precedence over environment settings. For a deployment managed with environment variables, the existing supported alternative is: environment: AI_PROVIDER: gemini AI_MODEL: ${MEALF_AI_MODEL} AI_INPUT_FORMATS: text,image,pdf AI_API_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/recipe_ai_key AI_TIMEOUT: "30" AI_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR: "20"  This is a configuration fragment, not a complete Compose deployment. Mount the key file through your secret mechanism, readable by the application's non-root account with no group/other permissions (0400 or 0600). Never commit its contents. AI_BASE_URL overrides the provider default; AI_MAX_CONTENT and AI_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT=1 are also supported.

sections.heading: Import and review
sections.text: Import and review Open Recipes → Import recipe. Choose a supported file, paste a public URL, or supply recipe text. Uploaded media requires AI and an explicit disclosure checkbox. Website imports can use metadata without AI. Review the provider/model shown before consenting. If settings change while a queued AI import is waiting, extraction stops for renewed review rather than silently disclosing content to a different destination or model. The preview is editable using the existing recipe editor, including ingredient ranges, units, preparation, servings, timings and instructions. Warnings remain visible. Saving uses the existing durable mutation/confirmation flow; duplicate submissions do not create another recipe. Incomplete previews need a title, named ingredients, servings and steps before confirmation. Cancelled or confirmed drafts cannot be resurrected by a late worker.

sections.heading: Input formats and limits
sections.text: Input formats and limits Input Support and limits Photographs/screenshots JPEG, PNG, WebP; single frame, at most 8 MiB and 16 million decoded pixels. EXIF/GPS/text metadata is removed; images are normalized to JPEG, maximum 2048px edge and 1 MiB. Use legible scans. HEIC, SVG, animated GIF/WebP are rejected. PDF At most 8 MiB; checked for PDF signature/termination and sent natively to an enabled document-capable model. No local PDF rendering or script execution. Encrypted, corrupted, unusually long or unsupported PDFs can be rejected by the provider. Website Public HTTPS HTML or JSON-LD only; at most 1,000,000 bytes, bounded redirects/fetch time, validated public DNS addresses and pinned connections. Metadata first; AI fallback requires consent. Video upload MP4 or WebM with a matching container signature, at most 8 MiB, Gemini with video enabled. The cloud provider must support its codec. First ten minutes only. Video URL Public youtube.com / youtu.be watch, short or embed URL with a valid video ID; Gemini with youtube enabled. First ten minutes only. No playlist ingestion or arbitrary provider-side URL fetching. Other social video Public structured recipe metadata when available. Otherwise supply permitted recipe text, screenshots, or a supported video file. No private/authenticated scraping, DRM bypass, download service, or automatic social-media transcription. Text At most 100,000 characters accepted; the selected AI configuration's UTF-8 byte limit defaults to 50,000. No silent truncation. AI requests default to 20 per household per hour (including probes), with a separately limited probe action. Imports are capped at 20/hour and uploads at 40/hour. Provider requests have a configurable 1–120 second timeout, an 8192-token output ceiling, and a 500,000-byte response ceiling. There is no automatic provider fallback that could duplicate charges or change the disclosure destination. App limits complement, rather than replace, provider billing/spending limits. Transient uploaded sources have a combined 128 MiB storage budget. Hourly maintenance removes sources older than seven days unless a queued import still needs them. Re-upload an expired source to retry. Local queued bytes remain on the device until accepted by the server; browser recovery exports include them as base64 media. Terminal extraction previews are pruned after 30 days; minimal replay receipts remain. Provider/model/error-code attempt metadata is retained for 90 days. Backups of the whole data volume may retain older data.

sections.heading: Add a model or provider
sections.text: Add a model or provider

sections.heading: New model
sections.text: New model Enter its exact identifier in settings, select the supported input formats, and save as default. No source change or model-version update is required. Test the actual formats you intend to use, and configure billing limits with the provider. Structured JSON support is a model/endpoint capability; leave its checkbox off when uncertain.

sections.heading: New provider adapter
sections.text: New provider adapter The common interface in src/aircooker/ai.py is: class AIProvider(Protocol): def extract(self, source: AIInput) -> ExtractionResult: ... def close(self) -> None: ...  BaseProvider.extract checks configured capabilities/limits and validates the extraction envelope. Implement the provider's wire mapping by overriding generate_input: class ExampleProvider(BaseProvider): def generate_input(self, source: AIInput, schema: dict) -> str: system, user = self.prompt(source, schema) Map supported media explicitly; reject unimplemented formats. if source.kind != "text": raise DomainError("ai_input_format_unsupported", 422) response = self.send( "/generate", {"model": self.config.model, "system": system, "input": user, "max_output_tokens": 8192}, {"Authorization": "Bearer " + self.config.api_key}, ) if response.get("complete") is not True: raise DomainError("ai_output_incomplete", 422) return response["text"]  Register the provider in provider_for, PROVIDER_ENDPOINTS, and PROVIDER_FORMATS; extend the settings provider enum and UI label/options. Keep existing adapters unchanged. Use httpx.MockTransport to verify request encoding, configurable model selection, capabilities, authentication, truncation, quota responses and invalid JSON. Never trust a provider's claim of schema compliance, include keys in prompt content, or accept model-supplied record IDs. The legacy extract_recipe(text) method remains for existing text integrations/probes; new imports use extract(AIInput) and the neutral extraction schema.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting and security
sections.text: Troubleshooting and security Symptom/code Action AI unavailable / ai_not_configured Enable a provider, specify a model and save. Check that environment variables are not being overridden by a saved disabled setting. ai_input_format_unsupported Enable the format only if this model documents support, or choose a compatible model/provider and consent again. ai_authentication_failed Check the saved key, project permissions, endpoint and billing. A changed destination does not inherit another service's credential. ai_rate_limited, ai_request_limit, import_rate_limited Wait for the provider/application window to reset; check billing and configured quotas. ai_timeout, ai_provider_failed, ai_invalid_response Check the endpoint/network and service status. Increase the timeout within limits if appropriate. Provider response bodies are deliberately not echoed. ai_output_incomplete, ai_schema_validation_failed The model truncated/refused or returned invalid JSON. Try a clearer/smaller source or a compatible model, or enter the recipe manually. ai_configuration_changed_review_consent Review the newly selected provider/model and resubmit with renewed consent. import_source_expired Re-upload the source. Source address/URL forbidden Only permitted public HTTPS content is fetched. Do not disable SSRF or TLS checks; use permitted supplied text/media instead. PDF/video rejected Check its real format, encryption/codec, size and selected model support. Renaming a file does not convert it. Video recipe incomplete Only the first ten minutes are analysed. Supply permitted text or short clips/screenshots containing the missing facts. The Fernet integration vault encrypts provider profiles in /data/config/ai-provider.enc; its key is in /data/config/integrations.key, with private file permissions. Protect the data volume and its backups together: encryption does not protect against an attacker who can read both files. Keep keys server-side, rotate compromised keys with the provider, and use provider-side spending limits. No keys enter IndexedDB, recovery exports, canonical recipes, application responses, or application logs. Uploads and extraction drafts require household authentication; browser mutations also use the existing CSRF checks. PDFs/videos have no public download route. Imported text and media are untrusted data: adapters do not enable tools or execute instructions found in a source. URL fetches retain private-address/redirect/TLS protections. Custom API destinations are trusted administrator configuration, not URLs selected by recipe content. Cloud providers receive the source you explicitly consent to send; their retention and training policies still apply. Obtain rights to import supplied text/media, avoid private screenshots, and review the chosen provider's terms before use.

sections.heading: Validation status
sections.text: Validation status Automated tests use synthetic recipe sources, mocked provider HTTP transports, and real local browser/API flows. They can verify encoding, validation, provider selection and review behavior without spending provider credits. Live provider/model/region compatibility and physical Apple-device behavior require separate validation with an administrator's configuration. This feature does not publish a Docker image or modify the independently pinned native iOS contract; update that companion deliberately before native adoption.

title: Bring! integration
description: Mealf can project the current household shopping week into a selected Bring! list. This is an unofficial integration, with no affiliation with Bring! Labs AG. Review Bring!'s curre

sections.heading: Bring! integration
sections.text: Bring! integration Mealf can project the current household shopping week into a selected Bring! list. This is an unofficial integration, with no affiliation with Bring! Labs AG. Review Bring!'s current terms and use a dedicated disposable list for compatibility testing. Live service compatibility has not been verified by synthetic connector tests. The backend stores credentials and contacts Bring!; the PWA does not receive those credentials or call the service directly. An installed app is not required to stay open after a calendar change has synchronised to the backend.

sections.heading: Connect an account and list
sections.text: Connect an account and list Sign in to the administration console at / and open Bring!. Enter the Bring! account credentials and save them. Saving alone does not verify login. Connect/retrieve the available existing lists. Select a list returned for that account and save the selection. Review connection and capability status before expecting automatic writes. Credentials are encrypted at /data/config/bring.enc using the installation's restricted integrations.key. Keep both in a protected full-volume backup. Disconnecting removes the saved connection and compatibility report without deleting existing Bring! items.

sections.heading: Why automatic writes can remain disabled
sections.text: Why automatic writes can remain disabled A successful account login and list retrieval do not prove that the unofficial API supports safe UUID-based changes. Mealf requires a current compatibility report matching the selected list UUID and the supported SDK. The current gate expects SDK 1.1.2 and a report no older than 30 days. The console cannot override a failed or missing report. The source checkout includes scripts/bring_compatibility.py. It is an explicit live experiment, not a runtime container command. It creates a unique test item, checks UUID-based replay/update/completion/removal and verifies existing items remain intact. It must run only against a dedicated disposable test list, with your deliberate consent to those external mutations. From an environment with the project's pinned Python dependencies, prepare private credential files and set: export BRING_EMAIL_FILE=/secure/bring-email export BRING_PASSWORD_FILE=/secure/bring-password export BRING_TEST_LIST_ID=REPLACE_WITH_DEDICATED_LIST_UUID export BRING_DEDICATED_TEST_LIST=YES export BRING_COMPATIBILITY_REPORT=/secure/bring-compatibility.json python scripts/bring_compatibility.py  Replace the paths/UUID, restrict the credential files and keep passwords out of shell history. Do not run this on a normal household list. Install a genuinely successful generated report at /data/config/bring-compatibility.json in the backend volume, readable by UID 10001 with restricted permissions. Do not fabricate or edit a passed report. A report for one list does not authorise a different list.

sections.heading: Shopping behaviour
sections.text: Shopping behaviour The backend uses the current Monday–Sunday week in the household time zone. It scales ingredients to servings, combines compatible metric units, excludes available pantry staples and skips meals using existing leftovers. Unknown/ranged quantities remain explicit; it does not guess density, translations or package weights. Include in shopping this week temporarily includes an available staple for that shopping period. It expires for the following week. Offline edits retain the week selected on the device, even if they reach the backend after rollover. The ownership ledger tracks the external UUIDs Mealf created. It never adopts manual same-name items and only updates/removes ledger-owned UUIDs. Purchased or manually removed requirements remain suppressed for that shopping period. Increasing an already purchased requirement does not silently recreate it; finer additional-quantity handling remains unfinished. A new week uses independent requirement identities.

sections.heading: Reconcile and troubleshoot
sections.text: Reconcile and troubleshoot Use the console's reconciliation action when available, then inspect queue/job status. Queued work is not evidence that Bring! changed. The worker retries temporary failures with bounded backoff and polls for purchases/week rollover. Repeated failures can become terminal; review the safe error code before retrying. If nothing appears, check saved credentials, list membership, selected list, report age, matching SDK/list UUID, outbound connectivity and the current household week. Never disable the capability gate to make an unverified connector write. External API changes and races remain live-service risks. Source: Bring! engineering guide and compatibility experiment.

title: Meal reminders
description: Mealf offers optional per-device Web Push reminders. They need a reachable backend, HTTPS, browser permission and connectivity. They are best-effort notifications, not offline alar

sections.heading: Meal reminders
sections.text: Meal reminders Mealf offers optional per-device Web Push reminders. They need a reachable backend, HTTPS, browser permission and connectivity. They are best-effort notifications, not offline alarms. Live push-vendor and physical iPhone delivery remain unverified by the automated receiver tests.

sections.heading: Enable reminders on a device
sections.text: Enable reminders on a device Open the signed-in PWA. On iPhone/iPad, first add it to the Home Screen using Safari and open the installed app. Go to Settings → Meal reminders. Choose Connect notifications and allow the browser's permission prompt. Enable meal reminders, select categories/times and save while connected. Use the test-send control and check both server status and the actual device. Mealf does not request notification permission on launch. Each browser device connects independently. You do not need an Apple developer account, APNs certificate, Firebase project or extra backend container. Browser/OS policy determines whether Web Push is available on a particular device. Changing a reminder form stores a local draft, including offline. Only an explicit connected save changes server delivery. A pending draft does not update another device. Disconnect removes the server and browser subscriptions; OS permission is managed in the browser/device settings. A revoked/expired session needs sign-in and reconnection.

sections.heading: Scheduling rules
sections.text: Scheduling rules Times use the saved household time zone, even while your device travels. Each enabled category gets at most one recorded accepted reminder per household date when it has an uncooked meal. The worker checks once per minute. Cooking, removing or moving a meal, disabling its category or signing out suppresses pending delivery when next checked. An externally accepted notification cannot be recalled. After an outage, reminders catch up only within 15 minutes of their scheduled time. Older reminders are discarded. Spring DST gaps shift a time forward across the gap; the autumn repeated time uses its first occurrence. Changing the time after acceptance does not send the same day's category again. Temporary failures retry with bounded backoff, respecting the delivery window and bounded vendor Retry-After. Eight unsuccessful attempts can mark a job failed. A 404/410 subscription requires reconnection. Last accepted by delivery service means the vendor accepted an HTTP request; it does not prove the device displayed a message. Standard Web Push cannot guarantee exactly-once delivery after a crash/retry.

sections.heading: Network and privacy
sections.text: Network and privacy Permit outbound DNS/HTTPS from the backend to the supported vendor endpoints: Apple: hosts under .push.apple.com. Chromium: fcm.googleapis.com. Firefox: updates.push.services.mozilla.com. Other endpoints fail explicitly rather than becoming arbitrary network destinations. TLS verification and public-address validation remain enabled. This outbound path is separate from your inbound Cloudflare Tunnel or reverse proxy. Notifications use generic English/German text and a date or Settings link. They omit recipe titles, ingredients and household names, but may still appear on a lock screen. The vendor can observe delivery timing and connection metadata. Web Push is optional; no subscription means no reminder traffic. The server generates its VAPID key and encrypts it at /data/config/webpush-vapid.enc. Subscription credentials are also encrypted. Preserve the database, config vault and installation key together in a protected volume backup. Household JSON/ZIP exports exclude notification subscriptions. Reconnect devices after a clean household import or when a recovered installation has a different VAPID key.

sections.heading: If a reminder does not arrive
sections.text: If a reminder does not arrive Check permission, installed-app support, Focus/battery settings, connectivity, server health, saved preferences, household time zone, an uncooked meal in the selected category and per-device delivery/job status. Reconnect an expired subscription explicitly. Do not treat successful synthetic tests or vendor acceptance as proof of background OS display. Source: reminder architecture, evidence and platform links.

title: Backup & recovery
description: Use portable household exports for moving household content, and protected volume backups for full disaster recovery. Neither includes work that exists only on an offline browser.

sections.heading: Backup & recovery
sections.text: Backup and recovery Use portable household exports for moving household content, and protected volume backups for full disaster recovery. Neither includes work that exists only on an offline browser. Export that device's pending work separately before recovery. Backup type Contains Does not provide Household JSON/ZIP export Household content, referenced photos, planning preferences and accepted-recipe counts Password hashes, sessions, integration keys, notification subscriptions or a complete installation snapshot Local SQLite snapshot Consistent database, including password/session data and durable history Separate photo files or configuration/encryption-key files Stopped-volume backup Database, media and configuration when the entire volume is included Unsent edits on disconnected devices Browser recovery export That browser's records, drafts, outbox, archives and available photos An automatically importable household archive or server credentials All of these can contain private household content. Restrict access and use encrypted off-host storage. The application does not automatically encrypt a CLI database backup.

sections.heading: Download a portable household export
sections.text: Download a portable household export Sign in to the administration console at /. Open Data and download the ZIP household export. Store it privately and record the server version that created it. Test importing a copy into an isolated, compatible installation before relying on it. The ZIP includes a versioned manifest.json and referenced media/<UUID>.jpg files with checksums. JSON export is also available through the authenticated GET /api/v1/admin/export API. The current household JSON format is version 3; ZIP envelope version 1 embeds that manifest. Older compatible v1/v2 JSON remains importable. Do not relabel an archive to bypass version checks.

sections.heading: Import into another household
sections.text: Import into another household Configure and sign in to the destination first, then use Data to import the supported JSON or ZIP file and confirm. This operation merges validated records transactionally. Duplicate entity IDs reject the whole import with 409; existing data is not overwritten. Destructive replacement is not implemented. Do not wipe an existing household to work around a merge conflict. Limits include 8 MiB JSON/manifest, 280 MiB ZIP, 10,000 entities, 5,000 media records and the 256 MiB stored-photo quota. The proxy/CDN can have lower limits. Malformed members, symlinks, mismatched checksums and unsupported archive encryption are rejected. Reconfigure integrations and reconnect browser notifications after a clean household import.

sections.heading: Create a consistent SQLite snapshot
sections.text: Create a consistent SQLite snapshot Choose a new filename; the command refuses to overwrite an existing output: docker compose -f compose.yml exec mealf python -m aircooker.cli backup --output /data/backups/household.sqlite3  For a source-build installation: docker compose exec aircooker python -m aircooker.cli backup --output /data/backups/household.sqlite3  This uses SQLite's online backup API, so the database snapshot is consistent while the server is running. The output file is mode 0600 and contains sensitive database state. Photo files and /data/config are separate and must be backed up as well. A snapshot inside the same volume will not protect you from losing that volume or host. Never copy only an actively written .sqlite3 file with an ordinary file-copy tool; WAL writes may be outside it. For complete recovery, stop the backend and make a protected backup of the entire local volume using your host's volume-backup tools. Include /data/config/integrations.key, the encrypted settings/VAPID files, media and database files together. Keep a private record of the matching image digest and Compose configuration. Protect Cloudflare connector credentials separately from the Mealf volume.

sections.heading: Restore a complete volume
sections.text: Restore a complete volume Preserve the current volume and stop all backend writers. Restore the complete backup into a separate local volume with UID/GID 10001 ownership. Start the matching application image against that volume, isolated from public traffic. Verify health, household settings, recipes, photos and plans. Use the interactive local password recovery command to revoke restored sessions before public exposure. Reopen public ingress only after verification, then sign devices in again. Downgrading a migrated database is unsupported. To roll back an upgrade, restore the matching pre-upgrade volume with its prior image. A lost encryption key prevents decrypting saved integration and push credentials; restoring only the database is not a complete recovery. An older database can have a different history from a surviving browser. Preserve browser recovery exports and use explicit history recovery; do not blindly retry old queues. If the VAPID key changed, disconnect/reconnect notifications on each device. Test the restoration process regularly; the existence of a backup file is not proof of recovery. Source: backup documentation and local CLI implementation.

title: Upgrades & maintenance
description: Mealf is a development preview. Review the release notes and implementation status for the exact image you are installing. Published-image checks apply to that image, not to later

sections.heading: Upgrades & maintenance
sections.text: Upgrades and maintenance Mealf is a development preview. Review the release notes and implementation status for the exact image you are installing. Published-image checks apply to that image, not to later source commits or every live external service.

sections.heading: Update a preview installation
sections.text: Update a preview installation Finish active browser edits and synchronise devices where possible. Privately export pending work from devices that cannot sync. Record the current image tag/digest, Compose files, environment and volume identity. Create and verify a complete pre-upgrade backup. In the existing installation directory, keep the :preview image and pull_policy: always from Installation, or choose an exact image tag from the published releases. Preserve your settings and volume. Pull first, then stop the old backend and start the new one: docker compose -f compose.yml pull docker compose -f compose.yml stop mealf docker compose -f compose.yml up -d docker compose -f compose.yml ps docker compose -f compose.yml logs --tail=100 mealf  If you use compose.tunnel.yaml, keep both -f arguments on these commands. Keep your existing project name, /data volume, ingress and any intentional custom port/command/healthcheck settings. Never start a second backend against the same volume. Never use down -v for an upgrade. For a source build, check out the intended revision, build it with docker compose build, then stop aircooker and use docker compose up -d in the same project. Review any Compose changes rather than replacing the deployment's configuration blindly.

sections.heading: Verify after the update
sections.text: Verify after the update Check the private and public health endpoints: curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:5152/api/v1/system/health curl --fail https://mealf.example.com/api/v1/system/health  Replace the example hostname; the local check applies to this site’s port-5152 configuration. A source build may use port 8080. Both should report {"status":"ok"}. Inspect startup/migration errors, sign in and verify the existing household, recipes, photos and calendar. Save a test change and confirm it survives reload. Check integration/job status instead of assuming external writes occurred merely because work was queued. In the PWA, finish edits, accept the update prompt and reopen the app as needed. Do not clear browser storage to update it. If setup unexpectedly appears, check the volume mapping before creating a household. See Troubleshooting.

sections.heading: Roll back safely
sections.text: Roll back safely A migration failure rolls back its transaction. Once a newer schema is committed, downgrading that database is unsupported. Stop the new backend, preserve its current volume, and restore the pre-upgrade volume snapshot with the prior matching image. Verify it privately before returning traffic. Devices may need sign-in and explicit history recovery after a database rollback.

sections.heading: Routine health and diagnostics
sections.text: Routine health and diagnostics The administration overview shows queue/import states, safe error codes, database/WAL size, photo usage and free space. Authenticated read-only diagnostics are also available at /api/v1/admin/diagnostics and /api/v1/admin/jobs. Do not share raw database dumps, credentials, recipe sources or unredacted logs in issues. Keep enough disk space for the database, WAL, photos, import sources, backups and temporary archive transfers. SQLite file size does not immediately shrink after logical cleanup. Do not delete WAL files, sync receipts or unreferenced photos by hand; an offline device may still depend on them.

sections.heading: Automatic and manual retention
sections.text: Automatic and manual retention The single backend worker runs bounded hourly cleanup. It preserves pending user work, sync replay/history proofs, Bring! ownership and photos needed by offline edits. Current source includes these conservative windows: Eligible data Window / condition Raw AI import uploads After 7 days, unless referenced by queued/running import work Confirmed/cancelled import previews and concluded source payloads After 30 days, with stable replay receipts retained AI attempt audit records After 90 days Eligible completed notification jobs After 30 days; required receipts remain Expired sessions without notification references After 90 days past refresh expiry Audit events 90 days Stale export/restore temporary files Older than 24 hours, startup-only safe selection Inspect extra cleanup candidates locally: docker compose -f compose.yml exec mealf python -m aircooker.cli cleanup --dry-run  Apply a bounded pass by removing --dry-run. For source builds use service aircooker with the source Compose file. Output contains category counts. This is maintenance, not full household deletion or guaranteed forensic erasure. Backups and exports have their own operator-managed retention; the application does not delete them for you. Source: deployment, retention policy and retention implementation.
